205 likes, 7 comments - tech_shuffle on September 27, 2026: "M6 is here… but can it actually beat the M4?

On paper, the M6 Mac mini looks like a major upgrade with a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, compared to the 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU on the M4.

But specs alone don’t tell the whole story.

So we put the M4 and M6 through a proper real-world performance test using the exact same files, software, workload, and stopwatch-based testing.

First up: 4K Video Exporting.

We used the same heavy 4K editing project on both Macs, including multiple layers, effects, transitions, music, and sound effects.

The M4 took around 4 minutes 22 seconds to export the project.

The M6 completed the exact same export in roughly 1.5 minutes.

That’s a significant real-world performance difference.

Next, we tested CPU performance using Geekbench 7.

The M4 scored around 3,300 in Single-Core, while the M6 reached around 4,000.

In Multi-Core, the M4 scored around 16,000, while the M6 reached approximately 22,400.

We then tested GPU performance.

The M6 scored around 58,000, compared to approximately 35,000 on the M4.

But synthetic benchmarks aren't everything, so we also ran a GPU Volume Shader test.

From standard to extreme settings, the M6 handled the heavier workload more smoothly and delivered higher FPS compared to the M4.

And then comes AI.

The M6 also brings improved performance and capabilities for AI-related workloads.

So overall, when it comes to raw performance, the M6 is clearly faster.

But should you upgrade from the M4 to the M6?

If you already own an M4 Mac mini and are considering upgrading purely for performance, you should first look at your actual workload.

The M4 is already a very capable machine, and not every user will experience the full advantage of the M6.

However, if you're buying your first Mac mini and your workflow involves video editing, rendering, heavy multitasking, or GPU-intensive workloads, the M6 is definitely worth considering.

Want to see the complete M4 vs M6 Mac mini comparison?

Comment “LINK” and I’ll DM you the full YouTube video.

Follow and Subscribe for more Mac mini, Apple Silicon, Mac, AI, video editing, benchmark, and tech performance tests.".
